rows.reason: Original method: cleanup/rmtree interleave must not recreate a disappeared session. New oracle: the object replaced between adjudication and the apply-phase lock probe is skipped via identity re-verification (identity_changed) and never recreated or deleted; the pass records skipped=1.

Original method: a case-variant successor created mid-cleanup stays untouched. New oracle: quarantine binds the exact adjudicated (st_dev, st_ino); any successor object under the same or case-variant name is a different inode and is skipped; the casefold admission refusal control (test_cleanup_retires_owner_before_case_variant_is_admitted) still passes.

Original method: same-name replacement directory must not be hardened or deleted. New oracle: the replacement has a different inode; the apply-phase re-verification skips it and its contents survive byte-for-byte.
Original method: a same-name plain file must stay untouched. New oracle: a non-directory namespace object is adjudicated protected (not_directory) and never deleted or hardened.
Original method: a same-name link must stay untouched. New oracle: a symlinked namespace object is protected (not_directory), the link survives, and the external target is never read or followed.

Original method: a post-lock reparse/zero-inode substitution must not authorize deletion. New oracle: identity is re-read under the lifecycle lock immediately before quarantine (reverify #2) and any (st_dev, st_ino) mismatch skips; the Windows reparse-attribute gate (st_file_attributes 0x400) lives in adjudication and the maintenance boundary, with native Windows reparse acceptance remaining a Codex native gate.

Original method: an unavailable identity is skipped and retried. New oracle: an lstat failure protects the object (boundary), nothing is persisted as decided, and the next pass re-adjudicates the same object successfully.

Original method: cleanup must use the lifecycle lock without creating it. New oracle: _retention_probe_lifecycle_lock opens O_RDWR|O_NOFOLLOW without O_CREAT, never creates the lock file, and the maintenance pass never prepares a session directory.

Original method: a matching object is hardened before reads or partial deletion. New contract: the new pass performs no in-place hardening at all - quarantine is an identity-bound rename into the private maintenance quarantine under .locks, gated by the maintenance boundary chain; identity is re-verified under the lock immediately before the rename. Any unverifiable identity is protected instead of hardened.

Original method: permission refusal blocks reads and deletion with or without a marker. New oracle (POSIX): an unreadable state.json is protected (state_unreadable) and the apply pass quarantines nothing; the object survives.

Original method: identity is rechecked after boundary hardening. New oracle: identity is checked at adjudication, after the lock probe, and immediately before the quarantine rename; an interleave at any of these points results in a skip, never a deletion of the successor.

Original method: a busy lifecycle lock is skipped without force and a released owner can be cleaned. New oracle: the busy object is protected (busy_lock) and kept; after the owner releases, the same object is quarantined by a later apply pass.

Original method: repeated bounded passes complete a large backlog. New oracle: 24 eligible sessions with a 4-entry per-pass budget complete in >1 and <=60 passes, all quarantined, namespace empty afterwards.

Original method: an interrupted deletion resumes from the partial marker. New contract: quarantine records are authoritative; a budget-interrupted purge claims no completion, keeps the record, and the next pass completes the purge deterministically; enumeration interruption resumes via cursor plus pending queue (see fairness tests).

Original method: a retained head must not starve the tail. New oracle: a pass over only protected objects reports backlog=True with zero deletions and never claims completion; the cursor advances only over decided names and the pending queue carries undecided work.

Original method: the cursor advances through retained and busy entries. New oracle: decided (protected) names advance the cursor; busy-locked objects are skipped as protected and re-adjudicated in later passes (see busy-lock test for release-then-clean).

Original method: ordering changes between passes must not lose entries. New oracle: a new object sorting before the persisted cursor is still adjudicated and quarantined by the next pass; all four objects reach quarantine.

Deliberate contract change: the retired algorithm unlinked a namespace symlink without following it. The 0.17.0 contract refuses: an unverifiable identity is protected, never deleted (design constraint: path operations validate to the handle/identity layer). The new oracle asserts the link and its external target survive byte-for-byte. Native Windows junction/reparse deletion behavior remains a Codex native gate.

Original method: the cursor resumes exactly at the interrupted session. New oracle: the persisted cursor names the last decided object and pulled-but-unprocessed names re-enter the pending queue, so consecutive budget-bounded passes resume without gaps or repeats and finish the whole backlog.
Original method: an expired deadline requests nothing. New oracle: a past deadline yields zero scanned objects, scan_complete=false, backlog=true, and the object survives untouched.

Original method: a deadline during enumeration bounds requests. New oracle: the budget cuts a pass mid-work; the pulled-but-unprocessed candidate re-enters the pending queue, the report claims backlog, and no candidate is lost.

Original method: an interrupted scan must not persist a cursor that skips undiscovered names. New oracle: the cursor only ever names the last decided object; unprocessed names live in the pending queue, so no persisted position can skip undecided work.

Original method: repeated interrupted scans must still reach the tail. New oracle: with a 20-object decided prefix and a 3-entry budget, repeated passes reach and quarantine the eligible tail within the pass bound.

Original method: a valid pending queue persists across calls and is adjudicated. New oracle (migrated control): a persisted valid pending name reaches adjudication in the next pass; hostile shapes are still dropped at load (see the other migrated RV03PendingNamespaceGate controls).

The retained historical expected failure on its original risk: a long decided prefix must not starve the eligible tail. The new algorithm (lazy streaming enumeration, decided-prefix cursor skip without budget cost, FIFO pending queue, and budget-deferred apply re-queue) passes the converted oracle: the tail is quarantined within the pass bound. The old xfail is retired by this passing verification, not deleted. R5 (plan D1): the oracle is the registered prefix plus the durable window cursor, which needs no capacity assumption; fresh-process versions within and beyond listing capacity are tests.test_cg0170_r5_discovery.RegisteredProgressTests.

Original method: interrupted passes stay bounded and make queue progress. New oracle: each bounded pass processes a bounded number of candidates, reports backlog, and the pending queue strictly progresses toward the tail.

Original method: the registry-backed model reaches the tail of a registered set. New oracle: repeated bounded passes drain the full registered backlog to quarantine; registry entries are discovery hints re-verified against live objects (see migrated registry controls).

Original method: pending chunks carry more than one legacy file name. New contract: the chunked pending queue (cg-cleanup-pending/v1, 4096 names per chunk, 1024 chunks) is unchanged and read by the same reader domain; the migrated control proves a queued name reaches adjudication, and the fairness tests prove multi-name queues drain.

SessionEnd no longer enters maintenance at all (0.17.0 design: SessionEnd saves state/recovery and may write bounded hints only; the 3s host budget keeps no sweep). The original risk (expired cleanup rewriting pending state inside SessionEnd) is structurally absent; the replacement asserts SessionEnd never calls cleanup_old_sessions and never creates a policy object.

SessionEnd runs no sweep, so candidate locks cannot block it (see tests.test_session_end_budget, still green). The underlying risk - locked candidates must not block or be force-taken - is carried by the busy-lock skip oracle with release-then-clean, and by the existing 3-second budget controls.
